items.headline: Isak edges Arsenal defenders as the standout Gameweek 10 captaincy call
items.summary:
Alexander Isak is the preferred captain for Gameweek 10 as Liverpool face a Crystal Palace side judged to be in particularly poor form, vulnerable to pressing and notably weak at defending set pieces. Erling Haaland is considered a less compelling armband option against Nottingham Forest: despite just one clean sheet, Forest rank well for shots, big chances and efforts in the box conceded, suggesting Manchester City may win without producing a haul. Arsenal defenders Riccardo Calafiori and Gabriel are viable alternatives, with Arsenal expected to shut out Hull and both offering attacking routes to points, but Isak carries the highest overall upside.

Calafiori is an attractive short-term buy and captaincy differential against Hull after avoiding midweek action, while Gabriel remains the stronger set-piece threat. However, Calafiori brings a medium-term rotation risk as Arsenal’s Champions League schedule intensifies and William Saliba returns to full fitness, so Van Hecke is preferred over an eight-week horizon because he is more secure for minutes. Arsenal’s defensive triple-up is again under consideration, with David Raya, Gabriel and Calafiori the immediate preferred combination; Kai Havertz is a reasonable one-week punt for managers using a Free Hit or Wildcarding next week, but is not viewed as a priority forward over Isak, Haaland, Barry or Evanilson.

The main transfer recommendation is Dominic Calvert-Lewin to Isak, especially after Calvert-Lewin misses training and with Leeds’ attack cooling. Liverpool’s trip to Palace also makes Virgil van Dijk an aggressive one-week defensive target, particularly for Ezri Konsa owners concerned by a possible knock and Saliba’s return. Van Dijk costs far more than Jarell Quansah, but Palace’s set-piece weakness makes his goal threat especially appealing this week.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a clear sell despite decent individual creativity, because Nottingham Forest lack reliable scorers and face Manchester City, Bournemouth, Chelsea, Hull and Brighton. Tavernier is the favoured replacement, with Everton midfielder Dewsbury-Hall another fixture-led punt against Coventry. At £5m, Rodon is narrowly preferred to Julio Enciso due to penalties and steadier output, although Enciso’s high shot volume, two goals and two assists make him a legitimate alternative alongside Balumi.

For Spurs coverage, Guglielmo Vicario, Van Hecke and Mohammed Kudus are viewed as the best three current assets. Van Hecke is a strong starter if Calvert-Lewin is absent, while Brighton’s Gross versus Brentford and Aston Villa’s Manzambi versus Manchester United are close bench decisions; Manzambi gets the nod for his direct goal threat, minutes and penalties. Managers are urged not to buy Brighton’s Dco at his apparent peak, with his role expected to weaken when Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh are fit again.
key_points: Captain Isak against Crystal Palace, with Calafiori and Gabriel the leading defensive alternatives; Haaland ranks behind all three for Gameweek 10.
Sell Dominic Calvert-Lewin for Isak, particularly after Calvert-Lewin misses training and Leeds’ attacking output declines.
Calafiori is an excellent Hull punt but carries Champions League-related rotation risk; Van Hecke is preferred for sustained security over the next eight gameweeks.
Morgan Gibbs-White is a priority sale because Forest lack finishing quality and enter an unconvincing fixture run.
Virgil van Dijk is a high-upside one-week buy against Crystal Palace due to their severe set-piece vulnerability, while Jarell Quansah is the better-value longer-term Liverpool defender.
Rodon is marginally the best £5m midfielder because of penalties, but Enciso and Balumi are strong budget alternatives.
Avoid buying Dco despite his form, as Mitoma and Minteh returning should reduce his appeal; keep him only while the points continue.
Start Van Hecke if Calvert-Lewin is ruled out, and favour Manzambi over Gross in close bench calls.

items.title: FPL GW10 Team Selection: Konsa Concerns & Free Hit Plans 🚨 | Transfers & Captain
items.headline: Haaland edges Calafiori for Gameweek 10 captaincy as Arsenal defence peaks
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the preferred Gameweek 10 captain against Nottingham Forest, with Riccardo Calafiori an attractive vice-captain punt after being rested in midweek. Arsenal’s home match with Hull is the standout defensive fixture: bookmakers give them a 58% clean-sheet probability, so David Raya, Calafiori and Concer are all started. The squad is set up in a four-defender formation, with Silva and D Kyper also playing; Kyper is expected to retain his advanced left-sided role and remains worth starting outside the toughest fixtures.

Concer is the main immediate concern. He comes off with a possible knee issue in Arsenal’s Champions League match, although he is still expected to start against Hull. Managers should not rely on the lack of an FPL injury flag and need a credible bench substitute. More importantly, William Saliba’s return puts Concer’s medium-term place at risk: Saliba is eased back after a long recovery, but could reclaim a starting centre-back role from Gameweek 11, particularly after the international break. Concer is therefore viewed as a likely sale by Gameweek 11 or 12.

The attack remains led by Haaland, Nicolas Jackson and Barry. Jackson is backed against Manchester United because United’s defence is depleted and continues to concede chances, while Barry is a value play at home to Coventry despite inconsistent finishing: his positioning and chance volume make him viable when fixtures are favourable. Bryan Mbeumo also starts against Aston Villa, as Manchester United’s midweek win may boost confidence and Mbeumo continues to get central, counter-attacking opportunities. Chelsea assets Cole Palmer and Rogers are started at Sunderland, but with limited conviction; Sunderland’s home defensive numbers are strong, making Palmer in particular a possible disappointment unless he benefits from penalties.

The planned move for Gameweek 11 is Concer to Viskovich, doubling up on Brighton defence for Hull and improving the bench for Mbeumo, Barry and Maherovic’s weaker fixtures. In Gameweek 12, Barry and Palmer could make way for Manzambi and Calvert-Lewin, targeting Ipswich and Coventry while avoiding an overloaded Arsenal defence for Manchester City away. Rather than Free Hitting in Gameweek 12, the chip is earmarked for Gameweek 13, when it can attack Liverpool v Sunderland, Chelsea v Crystal Palace, Spurs v Fulham and Coventry v Ipswich, while avoiding Bournemouth v Brighton and other awkward clashes between owned players. Chelsea assets, potentially Palmer and Joao Pedro, are then targeted again around Gameweek 16 when their fixtures improve and their lack of European football becomes an advantage.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Nottingham Forest, with Calafiori vice-captain and a viable differential captain against Hull.
Start Arsenal’s Raya, Calafiori and Concer against Hull, with Arsenal carrying a 58% clean-sheet probability.
Concer is expected to start in Gameweek 10 despite a knee concern, but Saliba’s recovery makes him a likely transfer out from Gameweek 11.
Target Concer to Viskovich in Gameweek 11 to add Brighton defensive coverage for Hull.
Start Jackson against an injury-hit Manchester United defence and Barry against Coventry, despite Barry’s erratic finishing.
Palmer and Rogers start at Sunderland, but Sunderland’s strong home defensive data makes Chelsea attackers less appealing than the league table suggests.
Maherovic is a credible alternative to Palmer if taking a risk, while Gross is benched after a sharp decline in his recent shooting numbers.
Plan to Free Hit in Gameweek 13 rather than Gameweek 12, targeting the favourable Liverpool, Chelsea, Spurs and Coventry fixtures.

items.headline: Haaland holds captaincy, but Calafiori clean-sheet appeal tests the Gameweek 10 call
items.summary:
A -4 hit reshapes the squad for Gameweek 10, with Bobby Thomas upgraded to Antonio Silva and Morgan Gibbs-White sold for Marcus Tavernier. The move creates double Bournemouth coverage, with Tavernier joining De Cuyper ahead of Ipswich, and is made with Bournemouth’s favourable longer-term fixture run in mind rather than as a one-week punt.

David Raya starts in goal behind an Arsenal double-up featuring Riccardo Calafiori, while the wider defensive options include De Cuyper, Ben Mee and Antonio Silva. Pascal Groß, Cole Palmer, Tavernier and Morgan Rogers make up the midfield, with Erling Haaland and Nicolas Jackson leading the attack. The structure is intended to be strong beyond Gameweek 10, even after paying four points to make the changes.

Haaland currently wears the captain’s armband, but Calafiori is a serious alternative at home to Hull. Arsenal’s clean-sheet prospects look especially strong, while Nottingham Forest’s lack of goals makes the defensive captaincy route tempting, although Forest have still been relatively resilient at the back and Haaland remains the safer high-ceiling captain.

The remaining selection dilemma is whether Jan Paul van Hecke, first substitute after a 15-point return last week, should start away at Leeds. The reluctance is to bench either Bournemouth player immediately after buying them for Ipswich, leaving Mee as the likeliest player to drop out despite also being a new signing. The decision comes down to backing Bournemouth’s fixture and long-term plan or chasing Van Hecke’s recent form.
key_points: A -4 hit funds Bobby Thomas to Antonio Silva and Morgan Gibbs-White to Marcus Tavernier ahead of Gameweek 10.
Double Bournemouth coverage through Tavernier and De Cuyper is targeted at Ipswich and Bournemouth’s strong upcoming fixtures.
Haaland is the current captain, but Calafiori is under consideration because Arsenal’s home clean-sheet chance against Hull looks excellent.
Raya and Calafiori provide Arsenal defensive coverage, with Calafiori offering an unusually viable defensive captaincy differential.
Van Hecke is first on the bench despite a 15-point haul last week and an away fixture at Leeds.
Mee is the main candidate to be benched if Van Hecke starts, even though Mee is also newly transferred in.

items.title: My Team Selection for Gameweek 10 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Haaland keeps captaincy as Gabriel fitness concern leaves Arsenal triple-up exposed
items.summary:
The Gameweek 10 squad stays largely unchanged after a 63-point return lifts the rank to 68,000. Erling Haaland remains captain despite Nottingham Forest away looking less straightforward than the fixture may initially suggest. Cole Palmer and Riccardo Calafiori are considered viable alternative captains, but Haaland’s armband is expected to stay in place.

The main selection concern is Arsenal’s defence. David Raya and Calafiori are expected to start, but Gabriel is a doubt after coming off early in the Champions League, with Mikel Arteta acknowledging recent fitness issues and William Saliba returning. Ezri Konsa is likely to replace Gabriel in the XI if needed, while Jan Paul van Hecke provides further bench cover. No extra transfer is planned purely to insure against Gabriel’s possible absence.

Lewis Hall is the player most in need of a sale, but he can be benched in Gameweek 10, allowing that decision to wait until Gameweek 11. Palmer and Morgan Rogers are both retained because their minutes remain secure and their fixtures are still favourable. Palmer is not viewed as outstanding value at his price, but with £1.9m in the bank and no pressing upgrade elsewhere, there is little reason to cash out.

Bryan Mbeumo is also held despite a recent dip in returns: he offers differential appeal and sufficient goal threat ahead of Aston Villa at home. The Brighton slot, identified as Pascal Groß, is an easy hold after difficult meetings with Liverpool and Manchester City, with a favourable fixture run ahead. Nicolas Jackson has only just replaced João Pedro and is not under consideration for a sale, while Haaland is a clear long-term hold. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is retained too, as his schedule continues to offer a playable fixture roughly every other week.
key_points: Erling Haaland remains the preferred Gameweek 10 captain, with Palmer and Calafiori only outside alternatives.
Gabriel is a fitness doubt after an early Champions League substitution, so Konsa is set to start if he misses out.
Raya and Calafiori are expected to be fit, while Van Hecke provides bench cover behind the Arsenal defensive trio.
No transfer is made to cover Gabriel; Lewis Hall is the intended future sale, likely from Gameweek 11.
Palmer and Morgan Rogers are held because of reliable minutes and favourable fixtures, with £1.9m in the bank reducing the need to downgrade.
Bryan Mbeumo is retained for Aston Villa at home despite recent blanks, given his differential status and attacking threat.
Nicolas Jackson, Haaland and Calvert-Lewin are all holds, with Jackson having recently arrived for João Pedro.

items.headline: Barry emerges as a captaincy contender as defensive investment drives Gameweek 10 plans
items.summary:
A 67-point Gameweek 9 is soured by 19 bench points from Konaté and Mendy, but the squad still delivers through Van Hecke’s 15-point haul, returns from Palmer, Rogers and Barry, and an immediate eight points from Silva. The key regret is starting Mendy at home to Ipswich rather than Konaté away to Liverpool, although Arsenal’s clean sheet at Anfield is an exceptional result rather than an obvious call in advance. Schade looks like the weak transfer after failing to register a shot, while Mbeumo retains patience because he is nailed, playing as a striker and posting encouraging underlying numbers.

The preferred Gameweek 10 XI is a 4-4-2: Raya; Konaté, Silva, De Cuyper and Van Hecke; Mbeumo, Palmer, Rogers and Gross; Barry and Haaland. Van Hecke is the marginal starter over Schade despite a difficult trip to Leeds, because the upside of defensive returns from both Van Hecke and De Cuyper is greater than relying on one Schade attacking return. Konaté remains worth holding despite Saliba’s return to Arsenal training and a minor knee concern in Europe; he is likely safe through the international break, but could become a sell around Gameweek 11 when Arsenal face Newcastle away and Manchester City at home.

Captaincy is still open. Haaland has a difficult match against a Forest side whose underlying defensive numbers are strong, and he plays 90 minutes in Europe. Barry is a serious alternative, with eight goals in all competitions and 6.37 xG, nearly matching Haaland’s 6.57 xG. Palmer and Rogers also have major upside against a Sunderland side hit by injuries and Europa League commitments, with Chelsea benefiting from a full midweek to prepare. Barry may take the vice-captaincy and is even under consideration for the armband.

With one free transfer and £1.3m in the bank, the leading plan is to roll. João Pedro could be moved to Calvert-Lewin or Jackson, but Jackson restricts future routes to Gabriel or Van Dijk, while Calvert-Lewin is attractive for Gameweek 12 captaincy. Holding João Pedro through this week could pay off if he returns in Gameweek 11 and matches Jackson’s output. Mendy to Vuskovic is also tempting because Vuskovic has Brentford at home, Hull after the break, strong DEFCON potential, set-piece threat and a solid defence behind him. However, Gross is one yellow from suspension and João Pedro remains a fitness concern, making flexibility valuable over the international break.

Gabriel remains the long-term defensive target, but buying him may wait until Gameweek 13 or 14 because Arsenal’s immediate schedule includes Manchester City and because Chelsea’s Gameweek 13 home fixture against Palace is a poor time to break up the Palmer-Rogers-Jackson/João Pedro core. If Konaté’s knee issue worsens, the move to Vuskovic is brought forward; otherwise, upgrading the defence after the break remains the likely route. Gross, Thiago, Maguire, Janelt, McBurnie and Ampadu are all one booking away from a one-match ban, while Rogers, De Cuyper, Tavernier, Calvert-Lewin and Van Dijk are two yellows away.
key_points: Barry is a viable Gameweek 10 captain or vice-captain after reaching eight goals in all competitions and recording 6.37 xG.
The Gameweek 10 team shifts to a 4-4-2, with Van Hecke and De Cuyper starting ahead of Schade for greater combined defensive upside.
Haaland remains in the XI but faces a Forest side with the league’s second-best expected defensive record after nine matches.
Mbeumo is a hold despite recent blanks because he is nailed as a striker and continues to post promising underlying numbers.
Konaté is held for now despite a knee issue and Saliba’s return, but could be sold around Gameweek 11 if his minutes or fitness become uncertain.
Vuskovic is the leading defensive transfer target thanks to his Brentford and Hull fixtures, DEFCON returns, goal threat and low price.
Rolling the free transfer is preferred over João Pedro to Jackson or Calvert-Lewin, preserving flexibility for injuries, suspensions and a later Gabriel upgrade.
Gross is one yellow card from suspension, increasing the value of carrying two free transfers through the international break.

items.headline: Haaland remains captain as Arsenal’s Kza injury concern tests Gameweek 10 transfer patience
items.summary:
A 63-point Gameweek 9 score brings a small green arrow from 72,000 to 68,000 overall, despite several awkward fixtures. Van Hecke’s 15-pointer against Crystal Palace and Arsenal’s unexpected double clean sheet at Liverpool provide the upside, while the move from Joao Pedro to Nicolas Jackson returns nine points. The key lesson is not to overreact to fortunate returns: Arsenal defenders remain sound assets even if a clean sheet at Anfield is unusually fortunate, and Lewis Hall was still a reasonable starter over Van Hecke on fixture strength.

For Gameweek 10, the preferred approach is to roll one of three free transfers and enter the international break with four. Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Pervis Estupinan are expected to start, with Arsenal at home to Hull and Brighton at home to Brentford offering defensive appeal. Kza is the genuine concern after being withdrawn in Europe with a knee issue, while William Saliba is nearing a return. Kza is not a buy now, but selling an owned Kza before the break also feels premature: if he misses out completely, Van Hecke is an acceptable bench replacement. Micky van de Ven? No, Lewis Hall remains a longer-term problem because Newcastle’s defence is unreliable, but there is no urgency to fix him this week.

The midfield is settled. Cole Palmer travels to Sunderland, Morgan Rogers faces Sunderland away, Bryan Mbeumo hosts Aston Villa and Pascal Gross hosts Brentford. Palmer remains expensive but is on penalties, has secure minutes and does not face European fatigue, making a sale unnecessary when there is £1.9m in the bank. Mbeumo’s recent blanks do not outweigh his strong minutes, chance creation and improving Manchester United fixture run from Gameweek 12. Gross, bought at £5.5m, is viewed as a hold while fit, while Sangare is simply third bench until a more pressing need emerges.

Nicolas Jackson starts away to Manchester United alongside Erling Haaland at Nottingham Forest and Dominic Calvert-Lewin at home to Spurs. Jackson is preferred to a benching despite the away fixture, while Calvert-Lewin stays ahead of Van Hecke because he is a nailed penalty taker at home. Joao Pedro is a likely future target, potentially replacing Jackson around Gameweek 16 when Chelsea’s schedule improves again, but there is no need to force that move now. Haaland gets the captaincy over Calafiori and Palmer: Forest are defensively capable, but Haaland offers secure minutes and a safe default armband, whereas Calafiori carries a small rotation risk.
key_points: Roll the transfer if possible, preserving four free transfers for Gameweek 11 after the international break.
Captain Erling Haaland away to Nottingham Forest, with Calafiori and Cole Palmer viable but less trusted alternatives.
Kza is a fitness and selection concern after a knee issue in Europe and Saliba’s return, but owners with bench cover should wait for Arsenal press-conference news rather than sell immediately.
Calafiori is expected to start against Hull after receiving no Champions League minutes, while Raya is fully secure and Estupinan is also expected to feature against Brentford.
Do not sell Palmer, Rogers, Mbeumo or Gross in Gameweek 10; their minutes, fixtures and price points justify holding.
Start Calvert-Lewin against Spurs rather than Van Hecke, prioritising his home fixture, penalties and attacking role.
Lewis Hall is a future sale due to Newcastle’s poor defensive form, with Vuskovic or Silva possible replacements, but the move can wait until after the break.
Joao Pedro is a planned forward target later, most likely for Jackson around Gameweek 16, rather than a transfer to force now.

items.title: FPL GW10 Expert Trends, Transfers & Best Captains 🧠 #fpl
items.headline: Isak emerges as Gameweek 10’s standout expert differential captain
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains the overwhelming Gameweek 10 captaincy choice among a panel of 100 FPL experts, taking 81% of armbands. However, Alexander Isak is the notable alternative: 9% captain him despite being owned by only 21% of the experts surveyed, equating to a striking 43% captaincy rate among his owners. That makes the Newcastle forward a credible high-upside captain over Haaland for managers who already own him, with Crystal Palace the immediate opponent.

Isak is also one of the leading transfers in, with eight expert purchases, and is presented as the premium forward target for managers able to afford him. Liverpool’s favourable upcoming fixture run is another factor shaping transfer plans, while Gabriel, Tavernier and Man Zambi also feature among the more popular arrivals. Antonio Silva of Bournemouth is the single most popular incoming transfer in the expert sample.

The main sales are concentrated in defence and midfield. Lewis Hall is the most widely transferred-out player, with 21% of his expert owners moving him on. João Pedro owners are continuing to sell, while Morgan Gibbs-White, Gonçalo Guedes and Bernardo Silva are also common exits. Evan Ndicka is not especially high on the transfer-in list, suggesting experts are not treating him as the primary defensive replacement.

For managers following the trends, the key decision is whether to take the safety of Haaland’s huge captaincy backing or use Isak as a more aggressive play in a favourable fixture. Buying Isak offers both a strong Gameweek 10 option and alignment with a growing expert move, but it requires the budget to reach him and carries more risk than following the Haaland consensus.
key_points: Haaland is captained by 81% of the 100 experts for Gameweek 10.
Alexander Isak receives 9% of captaincies and is captained by 43% of his expert owners ahead of Crystal Palace.
Isak is among the leading transfers in, with eight expert purchases, and is the main forward upgrade for managers with sufficient budget.
Antonio Silva of Bournemouth is the most popular expert transfer in for Gameweek 10.
Lewis Hall is the leading transfer out, with 21% of his expert owners selling him.
João Pedro, Morgan Gibbs-White, Gonçalo Guedes and Bernardo Silva are also prominent expert sales.
Liverpool’s upcoming fixture run is viewed favourably, while Gabriel, Tavernier and Man Zambi are also popular incoming options.

items.title: FPL GW10 EXPERT Transfer Trends & Best Captain! 🧠 100 Experts Reveal Gameweek 10 Team Plans
items.headline: Antonio Silva emerges as the experts’ Gameweek 10 defensive differential
items.summary:
Most of the 100 FPL experts favour patience in Gameweek 10, with 60% making no transfer and only 33% using one free move. Recent transfer activity and the international break before Gameweek 11 strengthen the case for rolling, while chips are largely ignored: only one expert uses Bench Boost and one uses Free Hit. A Bench Boost is only considered worthwhile for managers with a genuinely strong 15-player squad.

Antonio Silva is the standout expert transfer target. The £5.1m Bournemouth defender is brought in by more experts than any other player, lifting his ownership to 32% among the group despite roughly 3% overall ownership. Bournemouth’s improved defensive form and a trip to Ipswich make him an appealing differential, particularly for managers upgrading a non-playing or £4.0m defender. Lewis Hall is the most notable sale, while João Pedro is increasingly expendable because of his injury and the growing number of viable forwards.

Alexander Isak is the leading forward buy among the experts, ahead of the more widely popular Evanilson. Moves from João Pedro, Gonzalo or Wissa to Isak receive the strongest approval, although the extra cost can require funding elsewhere. Gabriel is the preferred premium Arsenal defender for the long term, especially at home to Hull, while Silva is the cheaper alternative for managers unable to afford Gabriel or already holding three Arsenal players. Other viable moves include Gibbs-White to Tavernier, with Manzambi a cheaper but lower-priority midfield replacement.

The expert template remains built around Raya, Calafiori, Konsa, De Cuyper and Milenkovic, with Silva replacing Hall as the fifth defensive option. In midfield, Rogers, Palmer, Groß and Tavernier remain the core, though Gibbs-White is close to dropping out of the template. Haaland, Jackson and Calvert-Lewin lead the forward structure, but Isak, Barry and Evanilson provide more variation. Captaincy is overwhelmingly Haaland again, while Isak is the only meaningful alternative: 9% of all experts captain him against Crystal Palace, representing 43% of his owners. Arsenal captaincy options attract only limited support despite the favourable Hull fixture.
key_points: Roll the transfer if your squad has no pressing issue, as 60% of experts make no move before the Gameweek 11 international break.
Buy Antonio Silva at £5.1m if you need a defensive differential; he is the top expert transfer in ahead of Ipswich away.
Sell Lewis Hall if possible, while João Pedro is an increasingly reasonable exit because of injury and stronger forward alternatives.
Alexander Isak is the experts’ preferred forward purchase, with João Pedro, Gonzalo and Wissa the clearest routes to him.
Gabriel is the best long-term Arsenal defender if affordable, while Silva is the main alternative for managers blocked by budget or the three-player Arsenal limit.
Consider Gibbs-White to Tavernier, with Manzambi a cheaper midfield option; Gibbs-White is losing his place in the expert template.
Captain Haaland as the clear safe choice, but Isak against Crystal Palace is the leading high-upside alternative for owners.
Avoid using chips in Gameweek 10 unless a Bench Boost squad is exceptionally strong; expert chip usage is almost non-existent.

items.title: THE BEST FPL GW10 FREE HIT DRAFT! 🃏 #fpl  #premierleague   #football #fantasypremierleague
items.headline: Haaland leads a Free Hit built around Arsenal’s defence in Gameweek 10
items.summary:
A Gameweek 10 Free Hit centres on a triple-up of Arsenal’s defence, with David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Gabriel selected to maximise clean-sheet and set-piece potential. Gabriel also carries the vice-captaincy because Arsenal’s defensive ceiling looks especially high. Maxim De Cuyper completes the defence, although the team can shift to four or five at the back given the current points output from defenders.

The preferred shape is 3-4-3, with Morgan Rogers retained for Aston Villa’s trip to a struggling Sunderland. Bournemouth’s attractive attacking fixture supports a midfield double-up on Rayan and Marcus Tavernier, while Pascal Groß fills the final midfield place. Eli Kroupi is an alternative Bournemouth punt, but there is concern that he may not be secure enough for a start; Jobe Bellingham is another differential option at home to Coventry.

Up front, Thierno Barry provides Everton coverage, alongside Erling Haaland and Alexander Isak, who faces Crystal Palace away. Haaland is the standout captaincy choice, offering the safest combination of minutes, goal threat and explosive upside in a week packed with appealing attacking fixtures.

The main Free Hit trade-off is between locking in Arsenal’s defensive strength and spending more on additional attackers, particularly from Liverpool, whose fixtures also merit attention. The draft favours Arsenal’s reliable defensive returns while using Bournemouth, Villa, Everton and premium forwards to target the best attacking match-ups, making Gameweek 10 a strong opportunity to deploy the chip.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 10, with Gabriel as vice-captain.
Triple up on Arsenal’s defence with David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Gabriel.
Start Maxim De Cuyper as the fourth defensive asset, with a back four or back five viable given defenders’ recent scoring.
Morgan Rogers is retained for Aston Villa’s favourable trip to struggling Sunderland.
Double up on Bournemouth midfielders Rayan and Marcus Tavernier; Eli Kroupi is a higher-risk alternative because his starting place is uncertain.
Thierno Barry covers Everton’s fixture, while Alexander Isak is selected for the away match at Crystal Palace.
Liverpool attackers are viable alternatives if funds are released from Arsenal’s defence or elsewhere in the squad.

items.title: FPL WATCHLIST GW10 WITH FPL HARRY 🔎 | KONSA, ISAK & KROUPI JR | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Bournemouth’s Tavernier leads the GW10 midfield targets as FPL shifts toward five-man defences
items.summary:
FPL managers are increasingly set up to field four or five defenders in Gameweek 10, with clean-sheet potential and DEFCON points making mid-priced defenders unusually reliable. Arsenal remain the premium defensive target, but William Saliba’s return creates uncertainty around Ezri Konsa’s place rather than Gabriel’s. Konsa is still worth starting if already owned, especially this week, but he is not a buy and may become a problem after the international break. Riccardo Calafiori is also a rotation concern if he starts in Europe. Gabriel is the secure, expensive route into Arsenal’s defence, although Raya plus cheaper defenders such as Antonio Silva, Mihailo Mudryk, Jan Paul van Hecke, De Cuyper and Vuskovic can offer a viable alternative structure.

Bournemouth’s fixtures are the major attacking draw, with only Arsenal away standing out as a poor match-up over a long run through to around Gameweek 30. Marcus Tavernier is preferred to Ryan because he combines goal threat with stronger creative numbers, set pieces and exceptional bonus-point potential. Ryan shoots more often but tends to take lower-quality chances and is less likely to collect bonus. Justin Kluivert’s return adds another appealing option, but he is not yet certain to start after a 22-minute comeback; his presence is expected to affect Kluivert and Evanilson more than Tavernier or Ryan. Evanilson is also a legitimate forward option, with his more central role and four consecutive scoring gameweeks supporting the case that he has improved on last season.

Cole Palmer remains underwhelming for his near-£10m price, dropping deep and producing only one double-digit haul so far, but there is little urgency to sell before Chelsea face Sunderland. His squad structure remains useful while there are few compelling premium midfield alternatives. Morgan Gibbs-White, by contrast, is increasingly expendable: his underlying creativity is solid, but Leicester’s forwards are not converting enough of his chances and his own shooting volume is limited. The recommendation is to prioritise a Bournemouth midfielder over Gibbs-White or an out-of-form Sharda, while Lewis Hall can wait another week if the intended replacement is van Hecke.

Up front, Erling Haaland and Nicolas Jackson are the preferred core, while Evanilson, Barry, Calvin-Lewin and Costulas are all acceptable third-forward choices depending on squad needs. Alexander Isak is a strong option and a viable captaincy contender, but his price and injury record make him hard to justify when cheaper forwards have good fixtures and comparable upside. Evanilson has an excellent home fixture against Ipswich but is not the recommended captain; Isak is among the leading captaincy options if owned. Managers are also urged to slightly downgrade the value assigned to penalty takers, as penalties are arriving far less often than last season and VAR appears less inclined to intervene on marginal incidents.
key_points: Start Ezri Konsa if you own him for Gameweek 10, but avoid buying him with William Saliba nearing a full Arsenal return after the international break.
Marcus Tavernier is the preferred Bournemouth midfielder over Ryan, thanks to more central positions, creativity, set pieces and superior bonus-point prospects.
Wait for confirmation on Justin Kluivert’s fitness and starting status before buying him; his return is more likely to reduce Kluivert and Evanilson’s upside than Tavernier’s.
Bournemouth’s fixture run makes Tavernier, Ryan and Evanilson attractive medium-term targets, with Arsenal away their only major concern.
Nicolas Jackson remains a strong forward pick despite his rising price, while Evanilson offers the best cheaper route into Bournemouth’s attack.
Alexander Isak is a credible Gameweek 10 captaincy option, but his premium cost is difficult to defend over Jackson, Evanilson, Barry or Calvin-Lewin.
Cole Palmer is not currently delivering premium-level hauls, but Sunderland’s poor defence means he is worth retaining for now rather than selling immediately.
Morgan Gibbs-White is a reasonable sale candidate because his team-mates’ finishing and his limited shot volume are restricting his returns.

items.headline: Alexander Isak emerges as the standout low-owned Liverpool buy ahead of Crystal Palace
items.summary:
Liverpool’s recent performances make their attack worth renewed FPL attention, despite debate around their shot numbers against Arsenal. Their attacking patterns look increasingly convincing, while the team is also among the league’s strongest defensive units, ranking third for expected goals conceded. With results and underlying form improving, their fixture run is beginning to become more appealing even if it is not flawless.

Alexander Isak is the clear priority over Liverpool’s alternative attacking options. Cody Gakpo, Barcola and Szoboszlai offer routes into the side, while Jaque is considered an attractive cheaper defensive alternative to popular budget defenders such as Vuskovic, Silva and Van Hecke. However, those moves feel like compromises when Isak is the player with the strongest combination of quality, form and upside.

A transfer from João Pedro to Isak is particularly tempting for managers with both the budget and free transfers available. Isak’s ownership is unlikely to rise sharply because many managers are short of transfers, may prefer cheaper striker pivots such as Nicolas Jackson or Evanilson, or simply lack a spare forward slot. That leaves a rare opportunity to buy an elite forward before he becomes widely owned.

There is little pressure to preserve funds for midfield alternatives: Bukayo Saka is injured, Cole Palmer has underperformed from an FPL perspective, and defensive options such as Gabriel can be covered more cheaply by Contra. Isak is therefore not only a transfer target but a viable captaincy punt against Crystal Palace, especially for managers seeking a high-upside differential.
key_points: Alexander Isak is the preferred Liverpool FPL asset, ahead of Gakpo, Barcola and Szoboszlai.
Liverpool’s improving attacking play and third-place ranking for expected goals conceded strengthen their appeal despite imperfect fixtures.
A João Pedro-to-Isak move is attractive for managers with sufficient budget and available free transfers.
Isak’s ownership may remain low because managers are constrained by transfers, budget and forward slots, or are choosing Jackson and Evanilson instead.
Isak is a credible captaincy differential against Crystal Palace.
Jaque is viewed as a cheaper defensive alternative to Vuskovic, Silva and Van Hecke.
Saka’s injury and Palmer’s poor FPL output reduce the need to save money for premium midfield moves.

items.title: 🚨 Saliba is BACK! 🚨 Is It Time to SELL Konsa? 🤔 FPL Gameweek 10 Preview 🔥
items.headline: Saliba return puts Mosquera and Calafiori under growing FPL rotation pressure
items.summary:
William Saliba is back in first-team training after completing 45 minutes behind closed doors, and Mikel Arteta says he is ready to play once Arsenal decide the timing is right. While Saliba is still more likely to return after the international break than against Hull in Gameweek 10, his availability makes Cristhian Mosquera a risky buy immediately. Mosquera may start against Hull, but Saliba is an elite centre-back who should reclaim major minutes, while Mosquera can also appear as a substitute across the back line. Gabriel remains Arsenal’s safest defensive pick for league minutes, albeit at a premium price, while Saliba himself offers limited attacking and defensive-contribution appeal for his cost.

Riccardo Calafiori remains a strong hold for Hull at home and Newcastle in Gameweek 11, but the congested schedule creates a real rotation concern from Gameweeks 12-15 and through Christmas. Unlike a defender who either starts or misses out entirely, Calafiori can deliver damaging substitute appearances, making him harder to cover from the bench. There is no need to sell before Hull, but managers should have a succession plan rather than assume he starts every match. Arsenal’s fixtures are less compelling after Hull, even if their defensive quality still gives them clean-sheet potential.

Captaincy is primarily Erling Haaland against Nottingham Forest versus an Arsenal defender against Hull. Haaland is the reliable default despite Forest posting strong defensive underlying numbers, while Gabriel or Calafiori offer a high-upside differential because Arsenal are overwhelming clean-sheet favourites. Calafiori is marginally preferred over Gabriel for open-play attacking threat if he is rested in Europe; if he starts and plays heavily in midweek, the minutes risk is too great for captaincy. Arsenal attackers Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz are less appealing captain options because their returns are less reliable and both carry substitution risk.

A Gameweek 10 Free Hit should prioritise triple Arsenal defence, Haaland, Thierno Barry and Maxim De Cuyper, with additional upside available from Bournemouth, Brighton, Chelsea and Everton assets. On a Wildcard, Raya and Gabriel are the secure Arsenal core, while Calafiori is a calculated upside pick rather than a certainty. Antoine Semenyo? No—Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier is the preferred midfield target for his fixtures and likely minutes, ahead of Justin Kluivert, whose regular early substitutions and the return of Evanilson’s competition reduce his appeal. Kevin Schade is not an urgent sell with only one or two transfers, but can be moved to Tavernier by managers carrying spare transfers.

The broader tactical recommendation is not to lock into a permanent 5-3-2. Defensive-contribution defenders raise the squad floor and can be bought as long-term rotation pieces, but the best formation changes week by week according to fixtures and available attackers. Four or five at the back is viable when defenders have strong fixtures, but managers should still play their best XI rather than bench quality attackers simply to follow a supposed new defensive meta.
key_points: Do not buy Cristhian Mosquera in Gameweek 10: Saliba is fit again and threatens his place from Gameweek 11 onwards.
Keep Calafiori for Hull at home, but prepare for rotation during Arsenal’s congested Gameweeks 12-15 and Christmas schedule.
Captain Haaland against Nottingham Forest as the safe choice; Gabriel or Calafiori are credible differential captains against Hull, with Calafiori dependent on being rested in Europe.
A Gameweek 10 Free Hit should begin with Raya, Gabriel, Calafiori, Haaland, Thierno Barry and De Cuyper, then target Bournemouth, Brighton, Chelsea or Everton upside.
Raya and Gabriel are the preferred Arsenal defensive picks on a Wildcard because they offer the strongest minutes security.
Tavernier is the standout Bournemouth midfield target for the upcoming run, while Kluivert’s early substitutions and potential rotation make him less attractive.
Hold Kevin Schade if short of transfers, but managers with three or more free transfers can sell him for Tavernier.
Do not force 5-3-2 every week; build a pool of reliable defenders and select the best formation according to each gameweek’s fixtures.

items.headline: Gabriel captaincy gains momentum as Arsenal’s Hull fixture reshapes FPL transfer plans
items.summary:
Arsenal’s home meeting with Hull in Gameweek 10 is the dominant FPL talking point, with Gabriel rated as the standout defensive target and a viable captain. Arsenal are projected at roughly a 60% clean-sheet chance and maintain unusually strong clean-sheet probabilities throughout the coming weeks. Gabriel combines secure minutes, set-piece threat and DefCon potential, making him more attractive than cheaper Arsenal teammates for managers who can fund the move. He leads the captaincy projections ahead of Erling Haaland and Alexander Isak, although Haaland away to Nottingham Forest remains the safer, high-ownership captain.

William Saliba’s return to training creates some uncertainty around Cristhian Mosquera and Riccardo Calafiori, rather than Gabriel. Mosquera has delivered 14, nine and 10 points across the last three Gameweeks, while Calafiori offers attacking upside, but neither has Gabriel’s apparent security. Managers with Mosquera, Calafiori or Piero Hincapie can hold for Hull, but should preserve transfers in case Arsenal’s defensive selection changes. A popular medium-term route to Gabriel is downgrading an underperforming mid-priced midfielder such as Morgan Gibbs-White to a cheaper enabler, then upgrading a cheaper Arsenal defender.

The forward debate centres on whether premium Liverpool striker Isak justifies his cost against the cheaper in-form options. Isak is an appealing differential at Crystal Palace after showing encouraging underlying numbers, but his minutes and fitness history make him less compelling for captaincy. Nicolas Jackson, Igor Thiago, Evanilson and Thierno Barry offer strong returns at a much lower price, with Barry particularly notable after continued big-chance involvement. The money saved at forward can be redirected into Gabriel, which is why expensive Isak ownership may become increasingly difficult to justify.

Brighton’s fixture swing also improves the appeal of their assets, with Brentford, Newcastle, Bournemouth, Nottingham Forest and Everton among the upcoming opponents. Yankuba Minteh and Diego Gomez are hold candidates, while goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen remains useful. Aston Villa’s Morgan Rogers and Evann Guessand/Jackson options are playable at Manchester United, but minutes are a concern for the cheaper Villa attackers after recent substitutions around the 60-65 minute mark. With strong squads and an international break approaching, the preferred approach is generally to roll transfers, build towards two or three free transfers, and reassess Gabriel moves afterwards.

Free Hit timing remains unclear because Arsenal’s defence is so reliable that even difficult fixtures can punish managers who sell or oppose them. Rather than forcing the chip for Arsenal versus Manchester City in Gameweek 12, managers can keep it for a week when several owned players are suspended, injured or facing poor fixtures. Yellow-card monitoring matters: Diego Gomez, Thiago and Harry Maguire sit on four bookings, while Rogers, Verbruggen, Tavernier and Dominic Calvert-Lewin are among several relevant assets on three.
key_points: Captain Gabriel against Hull if you own him and are comfortable backing Arsenal’s clean-sheet probability; Haaland at Nottingham Forest is the conservative alternative.
Gabriel is the preferred Arsenal defender for secure minutes, DefCon and set-piece threat, while Saliba’s return adds uncertainty to Mosquera and Calafiori.
Managers can hold Mosquera or Calafiori for Gameweek 10, but should bank transfers to react if Arsenal’s defensive hierarchy changes.
Avoid forcing an expensive Isak move solely for Crystal Palace away when Jackson, Evanilson, Barry and Thiago provide cheaper forward routes and protect funds for Gabriel.
Brighton’s fixtures improve sharply from Gameweek 10, strengthening the case to retain assets such as Minteh, Gomez and Verbruggen.
Morgan Rogers and Villa attackers remain playable at Manchester United, but reduced minutes for the cheaper options make benching them reasonable if stronger alternatives are available.
Consider saving the Free Hit for a suspension- or injury-hit Gameweek rather than automatically using it against Arsenal in Gameweek 12.
Monitor bookings closely: Diego Gomez, Thiago and Maguire are one yellow card from a suspension.

items.title: FPL GW10 Transfer Tips! | Buy, Sell, Keep, Avoid #fpl
items.headline: Bournemouth assets top Gameweek 10 plans as Bryan Mbeumo remains a hold
items.summary:
Bournemouth provide the main buying options for Gameweek 10, with the best choice depending on the position that needs fixing. Marcus Tavernier is the preferred midfield target, Evanilson is the forward pick, and Antonio Silva is highlighted as the standout defensive option outside Arsenal’s back line. Managers with a weak spot in their squad are urged to use Bournemouth’s form and attacking potential as the solution rather than forcing a like-for-like move elsewhere.

Newcastle assets are the priority sales. Lewis Hall is the clearest player to move on, while owners of other Newcastle options, including Barnes and Wissa, should also consider exits after a run of poor, directionless performances. The downturn is severe enough that Fulham players are considered playable against Newcastle in Gameweek 10, reversing what would normally be a difficult fixture.

Bryan Mbeumo is a recommended hold despite potential sales around him. Aston Villa are not convincing defensively, and their high line should suit Mbeumo’s counter-attacking threat. His chance creation and shooting against Chelsea indicate that returns are close if that level continues. Martin Odegaard is also a hold for managers considering a sale.

Avoid Ezri Konsa beyond the immediate fixture against Hull. Although the match-up is tempting, William Saliba’s return to training threatens Konsa’s centre-back minutes from around Gameweek 11. Even if he is used at right-back, he faces competition from Jurrien Timber and Ben White and loses much of the defensive-contribution appeal that comes with playing centrally. Current owners can use him for Gameweek 10 but should prepare a sale soon, while non-owners are advised not to buy into a short-lived opportunity.
key_points: Buy Bournemouth cover in the position needed: Marcus Tavernier in midfield, Evanilson up front or Antonio Silva in defence.
Sell Lewis Hall and consider moving on other Newcastle assets after their poor recent form.
Fulham players are viable starters against Newcastle in Gameweek 10 because of Newcastle’s current struggles.
Keep Bryan Mbeumo for Aston Villa, whose high defensive line suits his counter-attacking and shooting profile.
Keep Martin Odegaard despite transfer interest from some managers.
Avoid buying Ezri Konsa for the longer term, with William Saliba’s expected return likely to reduce his central-defence role around Gameweek 11.
If you own Konsa, use the favourable Gameweek 10 fixture if needed but plan an exit within the next week or so.
